title: Deploy SUZHI dApp on ICP: Internet Identity onboarding, sequential Citizen IDs, SUZHI ICRC-1 token, Proof-of-Contribution rewards, and token-based DAO + dashboard UI

requirements.text: Integrate Internet Identity (II) authentication in the frontend so users can sign in/out and the app can call the backend as the authenticated principal.

quotes: Integrate Internet Identity (II) for user authentication.

acceptanceCriteria: Users can sign in with Internet Identity and see their authenticated principal in the UI (or equivalent logged-in state).
All authenticated actions (onboard, create work logs, verify, transfer, create proposal, vote) are performed using the logged-in identity.

requirements.text: Implement a Citizen Registry in the Motoko backend that assigns each newly onboarded principal a unique sequential citizen ID (1, 2, 3, ...) and persists the counter and registry mapping in stable memory across upgrades.

quotes: Create a "Citizen Registry" canister that assigns every newly onboarded user a unique, sequential ID number (e.g., 1, 2, 3...) stored in stable memory.

acceptanceCriteria: Calling an onboard method as a new principal returns a new sequential ID starting at 1.
Calling onboard again as the same principal returns the already assigned ID and does not increment the counter.
After a canister upgrade, previously assigned IDs and the next ID counter are preserved.

requirements.text: Implement the SUZHI token in the Motoko backend following the ICRC-1 standard interface, with max supply = 1,000,000,000 and fully transferable balances between users.

quotes: Create a token called SUZHI with a Max Supply of 1,000,000,000 (1 Billion).
Ensure the token is fully transferable between users.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes the standard ICRC-1 query/metadata endpoints required for basic ICRC-1 compatibility (name, symbol, decimals, total_supply, fee, balance_of, transfer, metadata as applicable).
total_supply never exceeds 1,000,000,000.
Users can transfer SUZHI to another principal and balances update accordingly.
Transfers apply a configurable fee (defaulting to 0.0001 tokens worth in base units) and fail with a clear error when funds are insufficient.

requirements.text: Mint the entire 1,000,000,000 SUZHI supply at initialization to the provided owner Principal ID "[INSERT_YOUR_PRINCIPAL_ID_HERE]", and provide a safe way to set/replace this placeholder with the real owner principal before production use.

quotes: Minting: Mint the entire 1 Billion supply directly to my Principal ID: [INSERT_YOUR_PRINCIPAL_ID_HERE].

acceptanceCriteria: On first deployment/initialization, the full supply is credited to the configured owner principal.

If the owner principal is still the literal placeholder, the build includes an explicit, controller-restricted method to set the real owner principal once, and minting/ownership behavior is documented in code comments/user-facing admin UI copy.
Only the owner/controller can access any admin-only token distribution methods (e.g., bulk airdrop).

requirements.text: Add an owner-restricted bulk distribution method `bulkAirdrop(recipients: [Principal], amount: Nat)` that transfers `amount` SUZHI to each recipient in a single call (or batched safely) to quickly fund ~100 testers.

quotes: You can ask Caffeine AI to add a "Bulk Transfer" function: Function: bulkAirdrop(recipients: [Principal], amount: Nat)

acceptanceCriteria: Only the configured token owner (or canister controller, as defined) can call bulkAirdrop successfully.
If any transfer cannot be completed (e.g., insufficient owner balance), the method returns a clear error (and does not silently partially apply without indicating which transfers succeeded/failed).
Airdropped balances are immediately visible via balance_of.

requirements.text: Implement Proof of Contribution: allow users to create work logs in four categories (Physical, Knowledge, Creative, Wellness) and require exactly 2 peer verifications (unique verifiers, not the worker) before the backend automatically transfers SUZHI tokens to the worker.

quotes: Build a system where users log work in four categories: Physical, Knowledge, Creative, and Wellness.
Implement a logic where a work log requires 2 peer verifications before a smart contract automatically triggers a SUZHI token transfer to the worker.

acceptanceCriteria: Frontend provides a form to submit a work log with category and required fields (at minimum: description and time spent).
Backend stores work logs and their verification state in stable memory.
A work log can be verified by principals other than the worker; the same verifier cannot verify the same work log twice.
When the second valid verification is recorded, the reward is transferred automatically and the work log is marked as rewarded (cannot be rewarded again).
Frontend shows pending logs, verification count (0/2, 1/2, 2/2), and rewarded status.

requirements.text: Define a deterministic reward calculation for verified work logs and make the parameters configurable by an admin/owner (e.g., per-category base rate and/or per-hour rate), then use it for the automatic SUZHI reward transfer.

quotes: Once verified, smart contracts automatically calculate appropriate SUZHI tokens based on work type, skill level, and time invested.

acceptanceCriteria: Reward amount for a log is computed deterministically from stored log fields and current config.
Admin/owner can update reward parameters via a restricted method; non-admin calls are rejected.
Reward amount used for a given work log is recorded (so the UI can display what was paid).

requirements.text: Implement a DAO system in the Motoko backend for One Token, One Vote with: proposal submission (description, budget, timeline), a 7-day discussion period, a 5-day voting period, and automatic execution for proposals approved by >50% of votes.

quotes: Implement a DAO Canister for "One Token, One Vote."
Features: Proposal submission (description, budget, timeline), a 7-day discussion period, and a 5-day voting period.
Execution: Approved proposals (>50% vote) must execute automatically via smart contracts.

acceptanceCriteria: Users can create proposals containing description, budget, and timeline.
Each proposal enforces timing: discussion phase lasts 7 days from creation; voting phase lasts the next 5 days; votes outside voting phase are rejected.
Voting power is proportional to SUZHI token holdings (document whether balance is measured at vote time or snapshotted; implementation must be consistent and testable).

Proposal outcome is computed at the end of the voting phase; if approval is >50% (clearly defined in code—e.g., yesVotes > noVotes and yesVotes / (yesVotes+noVotes) > 0.5), proposal is marked approved.

Approved proposals execute automatically with an on-chain effect (at minimum: mark executed + perform a deterministic action such as transferring the proposal budget from a defined DAO treasury/owner account to a specified recipient/creator).
Frontend includes a Governance Portal to list proposals, view details (including phase countdowns), submit proposals, and cast votes.

requirements.text: Build the SUZHI dashboard UI with the specified Gold (#D4AF37), Brown (#4B3621), and Earthy (#C2B280) palette, and include the following sections: User Profile (show principal + unique citizen ID), Token Wallet (balance + transfer + optional buy placeholder), Contribution Logger (create/view/verify logs), and Governance Portal (view/submit/vote). All user-facing text must be in English.

quotes: Design a dashboard using a Gold (#D4AF37), Brown (#4B3621), and Earthy (#C2B280) color palette.
Layout: User Profile (with Unique ID), Token Wallet, Contribution Logger, and a Governance Portal to view/vote on proposals.
Use English for any user-facing text in the build request.

acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard uses the specified palette consistently across navigation, background, buttons, and typography.
User Profile section shows the assigned sequential Citizen ID after onboarding.
Token Wallet section shows SUZHI balance and enables transfer to another principal.
Contribution Logger allows creating logs and verifying others’ logs where permitted.
Governance Portal lists proposals and supports proposal creation and voting with phase indicators.

requirements.text: Apply a coherent 'eco-city' visual theme consistent with the gold/brown/earthy palette (typography, spacing, components styling) across the app without introducing new product features.

quotes: To get that "Eco-City" feel... Make the background a deep earthy brown, use gold gradients for the 'Access DAO' buttons, and use a clean, high-contrast white or sand color for the text.

acceptanceCriteria: Primary CTAs use gold accents/gradients and remain accessible (sufficient contrast).
Background and surfaces use earthy browns/tans with readable sand/white text.
Styling is consistent across all dashboard sections (no mixed, unrelated themes).

constraints: Backend must be implemented as a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo (no multi-canister backend architecture).
Only Internet Identity is used for authentication (no third-party auth providers).

Frontend immutable paths must not be edited: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui (compose these components/hooks instead).
nonGoals: Providing an off-chain or third-party payment flow for users to 'buy' SUZHI tokens (no Stripe or external checkout unless explicitly requested later).
Integrating external databases or non-ICP hosting providers.
Implementing real-time chat, push notifications, or WebSocket-based features.
Supporting external Web3 wallets like MetaMask/WalletConnect.
